title: An Arms Race Quietly Unfolds in Space

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是 Benjamin Poulin，我是 Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当 DJ 的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着 300 件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《The Reframers》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的 Michael Barbaro。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》（The Daily）。

sentences.en: Today, U.S.
sentences.zh: 今天，美国

sentences.en: officials now acknowledge a growing fear that Russia may be trying to put a nuclear weapon into Earth's orbit.
sentences.zh: 官员们承认，他们越来越担心俄罗斯可能正试图将核武器送入地球轨道。

sentences.en: But as my colleague Eric Lipton explains, their real worry is that America could lose the battle for military supremacy in space.
sentences.zh: 但正如我的同事 Eric Lipton 所解释的那样，他们真正担心的是美国可能会输掉这场太空军事霸权之争。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, February 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 2 月 28 日，星期三。

sentences.en: Eric, this story began in a pretty unusual way.
sentences.zh: Eric，这个故事的开端非常不同寻常。

sentences.en: I actually watched it unfold on social media in real time.
sentences.zh: 我实际上是在社交媒体上实时目睹了它的发酵。

sentences.en: And it started with a very cryptic message from a member of Congress.
sentences.zh: 它始于一位国会议员发布的一条非常隐晦的信息。

sentences.en: So just tell us about that.
sentences.zh: 所以，给我们讲讲这件事吧。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: Well, Representative Mike Turner, who's chairman of the House Intelligence Committee, put out a message saying,
sentences.zh: 众议院情报委员会主席 Mike Turner 众议员发布了一条消息，称：

sentences.en: Today, the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence has made available to all members of Congress information.
sentences.zh: 今天，众议院常设情报特别委员会已向所有国会议员提供了相关信息。

sentences.en: That he had information concerning a serious national security threat.
sentences.zh: 他掌握了有关严重国家安全威胁的情报。

sentences.en: And it was an unusual kind of a statement from the chairman of the House Intelligence Committee.
sentences.zh: 对于众议院情报委员会主席来说，这是一种不同寻常的声明。

sentences.en: I'm requesting that President Biden declassify all information relating to this threat so that Congress, the administration, and our allies...
sentences.zh: 我要求拜登总统解密所有与此威胁相关的信息，以便国会、政府以及我们的盟友……

sentences.en: And so he didn't really tell us what this was about, but he...
sentences.zh: 所以他并没有真正告诉我们这是关于什么的，但他……

sentences.en: He just told us to be very scared.
sentences.zh: 他只是告诉我们要非常害怕。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it immediately set off a scramble of national security reporters to try to figure out what that message meant.
sentences.zh: 这立即引发了国家安全记者们的争相报道，试图弄清楚那条信息意味着什么。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And pretty quickly...
sentences.zh: 而且很快……

sentences.en: Congressman Turner is referring to a foreign military capability, and that foreign military is the Russian military.
sentences.zh: Turner 议员指的是一种外国军事能力，而那个外国军队就是俄罗斯军队。

sentences.en: Reporters heard that this had to do with Russia and with a new type of military threat.
sentences.zh: 记者们听说这与俄罗斯有关，且涉及一种新型军事威胁。

sentences.en: And what exactly was this new kind of military threat?
sentences.zh: 那么这种新型军事威胁到底是什么？

sentences.en: The intelligence that our New York Times colleagues have collected is that Russia is preparing to put a weapon in space that would blow up a nuclear device.
sentences.zh: 我们《纽约时报》同事收集的情报显示，俄罗斯正准备在太空中部署一种能够引爆核装置的武器。

sentences.en: And when it did that, it would be used to target United States surveillance satellites.
sentences.zh: 一旦实施，它将被用来针对美国的监视卫星。

sentences.en: So here, we need to slow down and explain what that means, why it's so alarming, why nukes would ever be in space.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们需要放慢节奏，解释一下这意味着什么，为什么它如此令人担忧，以及为什么核武器会出现在太空中。

sentences.en: So just kind of disentangle all of that.
sentences.zh: 请帮我们理清这一切。

sentences.en: I think that few Americans realize just how vital space is to the military defense of the United States.
sentences.zh: 我认为很少有美国人意识到太空对美国国防有多么重要。

sentences.en: For decades, the United States has been building, effectively, school bus-sized satellites that cost massive amounts of money.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，美国一直在制造实际上有校车那么大、耗资巨大的卫星。

sentences.en: They're these exquisite systems that just sit there in space and provide incredible information.
sentences.zh: 它们是那些精密的系统，静静地悬浮在太空中，提供着难以置信的信息。

sentences.en: And we rely upon all of the assets that we have for navigation, for communication, for missile defense, for missile targeting.
sentences.zh: 我们依赖所拥有的所有资产来进行导航、通信、导弹防御和导弹瞄准。

sentences.en: And it's something that is one of the great powers of the United States is to have all of this equipment floating around above us.
sentences.zh: 拥有所有这些漂浮在我们头顶的设备，是美国强大的力量来源之一。

sentences.en: But the real flaw in the United States military space system is that there aren't very many of them.
sentences.zh: 但美国军事太空系统的真正缺陷在于，它们的数量并不多。

sentences.en: And you don't have to take out too many of them to severely disable the United States capacities.
sentences.zh: 你不需要摧毁太多，就能严重削弱美国的能力。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So back to this Congressman Turner and his message.
sentences.zh: 回到 Turner 议员和他的那条消息。

sentences.en: Why would the Russians need a nuclear element to their efforts to challenge America's satellite programs in space?
sentences.zh: 为什么俄罗斯在挑战美国太空卫星计划时，需要动用核元素？

sentences.en: Russia sees potentially a nuclear weapon as a way to take out large numbers of satellites in an instant.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯认为，核武器可能是一种瞬间摧毁大量卫星的方法。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It would fry them.
sentences.zh: 它会烧毁它们。

sentences.en: It would destroy them.
sentences.zh: 它会摧毁它们。

sentences.en: It would create all kinds of debris in space.
sentences.zh: 它会在太空中制造各种碎片。

sentences.en: And I think what's really going on here is the Russians in the early stages of their invasion of Ukraine were really frustrated that they were not able to really block the ability of the Ukrainian military to continue to communicate.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里真正发生的是，俄罗斯在入侵乌克兰的初期，因为无法阻止乌克兰军队继续通信而感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: And that's because the Ukrainian military was relying on SpaceX and Elon Musk and his network of Starlink satellites to continue to operate.
sentences.zh: 这是因为乌克兰军队依赖 SpaceX、埃隆·马斯克及其星链（Starlink）卫星网络来维持作战。

sentences.en: And it was actually in late 2022 when the Russians said, you know what, those American satellites are getting in our way and we may choose to target those satellites in the future.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在 2022 年底，俄罗斯就曾表示，那些美国卫星挡了我们的路，未来我们可能会选择针对这些卫星。

sentences.en: And I think that's what might be going on right now.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能就是现在正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So Russia has decided that a way for it to achieve any kind of military advantage over the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以俄罗斯认为，要获得对美国的任何军事优势，

sentences.en: and have success in things like its invasion of Ukraine is to be able to threaten the United States' satellite infrastructure in space in such a way that might make it hard for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 并在入侵乌克兰等行动中取得成功，一种方法就是威胁美国的太空卫星基础设施，使其难以

sentences.en: to effectively fight back against Russia.
sentences.zh: 有效地反击俄罗斯。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, on the ground,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在地面上，

sentences.en: Russia's been using what they call GPS jammers to disrupt the signals from satellites that are coming down in Ukraine on the ground as they're fighting the war.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯一直在使用他们所谓的 GPS 干扰器，在乌克兰战场上干扰来自卫星的信号。

sentences.en: But everything from the location of the soldier on the ground to when there's a missile that's launched that's targeted in the United States to how a ship communicates with another ship,
sentences.zh: 但从地面士兵的位置，到美国瞄准的导弹发射时间，再到舰船之间的通信，

sentences.en: everything goes through space.
sentences.zh: 一切都通过太空进行。

sentences.en: And I think that's one of the weakest points that the United States has, and it's the ability to mess up or disable their space-based communications, targeting, surveillance.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是美国最薄弱的环节之一，即干扰或瘫痪其基于太空的通信、瞄准和监视的能力。

sentences.en: You're saying that when a rival like Russia thinks about how it could actually and efficiently take out America's eyes and ears of our entire military,
sentences.zh: 你是说，当像俄罗斯这样的竞争对手思考如何真正有效地拔掉美国整个军队的“眼睛和耳朵”时，

sentences.en: it turns out there's really only one answer, and that's by doing it in space.
sentences.zh: 结果发现只有一个答案，那就是在太空中动手。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter how big and powerful the weapons systems are.
sentences.zh: 无论武器系统有多大、多强大，

sentences.en: If they can't target and they can't communicate, they're basically useless.
sentences.zh: 如果它们无法瞄准，无法通信，它们基本上就没用了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So if you believe that Russia could put a nuclear weapon in space that could hurt our ability to have eyes and ears on what they're doing, that would be very scary.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你认为俄罗斯可能在太空中部署核武器，从而损害我们监视他们行动的能力，那确实非常可怕。

sentences.en: But how confident are we that Vladimir Putin can, in fact, put a nuclear weapon in space that's capable of doing that?
sentences.zh: 但我们有多大把握认为弗拉基米尔·普京真的能把具备这种能力的核武器送入太空？

sentences.en: Given that, in fact, there's already been nuclear tests in space in the 1960s, the idea of them doing this is not out of the realm of technical possibilities.
sentences.zh: 考虑到 20 世纪 60 年代已经在太空中进行过核试验，他们这样做在技术上并非不可能。

sentences.en: It would be a violation of an international treaty, but Russia hasn't shown much concern about violating international treaties.
sentences.zh: 这会违反国际条约，但俄罗斯对违反国际条约似乎并不怎么担心。

sentences.en: So I don't think technically it would be that much of a challenge.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在技术上这不会是一个太大的挑战。

sentences.en: It would destabilize the world because suddenly you'd have nuclear weapons in space, and it would cross a line that so far no one has crossed.
sentences.zh: 这会破坏世界稳定，因为突然间太空中就有了核武器，这将跨越迄今为止无人敢跨越的红线。

sentences.en: But the notion, can it be done?
sentences.zh: 但关于“能否做到”这个概念，

sentences.en: I think it could be done.
sentences.zh: 我认为是可以做到的。

sentences.en: And I guess the question is not just can it be done, but how confident is the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我想问题不仅在于能否做到，还在于美国有多大把握

sentences.en: that Russia intends to do it, and how quickly?
sentences.zh: 认为俄罗斯打算这样做，以及速度会有多快？

sentences.en: That's really unclear, and I think that there's a lot of speculation even about exactly what this weapon might be.
sentences.zh: 这一点非常不明确，我认为即使对于这种武器到底是什么，也存在很多猜测。

sentences.en: It could be a nuclear-powered anti-satellite device that blows out satellites, but just be nuclear-powered.
sentences.zh: 它可能是一种核动力反卫星装置，能摧毁卫星，但只是核动力的。

sentences.en: It could be a nuclear weapon in space that explodes and blows out anything anywhere nearby.
sentences.zh: 它也可能是在太空中爆炸并摧毁附近任何物体的核武器。

sentences.en: And we don't know when this potential Russian weapon is going to go up into orbit, or whether or not, in fact, it ever really will.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道这种潜在的俄罗斯武器何时会进入轨道，或者它是否真的会进入轨道。

sentences.en: But what this does show a bit is that it's a bit of a Hail Mary by Russia,
sentences.zh: 但这确实表明，这有点像是俄罗斯的“孤注一掷”，

sentences.en: a way to try to exert its influence in space at a moment when Russia is actually a declining power relative to the other nations in the world.
sentences.zh: 在俄罗斯相对于世界其他国家而言正在衰落的时刻，试图以此在太空中施加影响。

sentences.en: Just explain that.
sentences.zh: 请解释一下。

sentences.en: How can Russia be a declining power right now in space?
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯现在怎么会是太空中的衰落力量？

sentences.en: Russia is not launching nearly as frequently as it had been, and its whole infrastructure around building new satellites is in decline,
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯的发射频率远不如从前，其围绕建造新卫星的整个基础设施都在衰落，

sentences.en: particularly compared to China, which is launching at a crazy pace right now and putting up all kinds of new commercial communication systems,
sentences.zh: 特别是与中国相比，中国目前的发射速度非常惊人，正在部署各种新型商业通信系统，

sentences.en: but also devices that could become offensive weapons against the United States.
sentences.zh: 以及可能成为针对美国进攻性武器的装置。

sentences.en: So at the end of the day, when I talk to people at the Pentagon, despite the noise that Russia is making about potentially putting a nuclear weapon in space,
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，当我与五角大楼的人交谈时，尽管俄罗斯在炒作可能在太空中部署核武器，

sentences.en: the biggest threat to the United States in space is actually China.
sentences.zh: 但美国在太空中面临的最大威胁实际上是中国。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是 Benjamin Poulin。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是 Mark Ronson。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当 DJ 的黑胶唱片时代，你每晚都要带着 300 件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《The Reframers》。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33 位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨 4 点 30 分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 七十年的太空探索。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60 款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟中最强的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝 175 年来帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，获取 nytimes.com/subscribe 的特别优惠。

sentences.en: So, Eric, we started off talking about the threat that it seemed Russia posed to the United States because of its willingness to potentially put a nuclear weapon in space.
sentences.zh: 那么，Eric，我们开头谈到了俄罗斯因可能在太空中部署核武器而对美国构成的威胁。

sentences.en: Now, you're saying that for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 现在，你说对于美国

sentences.en: military, the real threat in space is China.
sentences.zh: 军方来说，太空中的真正威胁是中国。

sentences.en: So, just explain that.
sentences.zh: 请解释一下。

sentences.en: China, as of at least the last decade, as part of an overall significant surge in its military capacity, space has been an incredibly intense focus.
sentences.zh: 至少在过去十年里，作为其整体军事能力显著提升的一部分，中国一直将太空作为极其核心的重点。

sentences.en: It has been launching at a really rapid pace, far ahead of Russia.
sentences.zh: 它的发射速度非常快，远远领先于俄罗斯。

sentences.en: And it's not only putting communication satellites up there, but it's putting systems that could potentially grab onto, move, and disable American military satellites.
sentences.zh: 它不仅在部署通信卫星，还在部署能够抓取、移动和瘫痪美国军事卫星的系统。

sentences.en: Well, how does that work?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, how does something that they launch into space grab onto an American satellite?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们发射到太空的东西怎么能抓取美国卫星？

sentences.en: Well, in January 2022, China put a satellite into space that had an arm that reached out and grabbed another satellite that was there in geosynchronous orbit.
sentences.zh: 2022 年 1 月，中国发射了一颗卫星，它带有一只机械臂，伸出来抓住了地球同步轨道上的另一颗卫星。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And it dragged it to a different location.
sentences.zh: 然后把它拖到了另一个位置。

sentences.en: So, basically, they found a way to put a tow truck up in space and showed that if they wanted to, they could move any satellite.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他们找到了一种在太空中部署“拖车”的方法，并证明了如果他们愿意，他们可以移动任何卫星。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They showed that they had the ability to not only send satellites up there, but to send trucks that had the capacity to grab onto maybe an enemy's, you know, surveillance system
sentences.zh: 他们证明了自己不仅有能力把卫星送上去，还有能力送上能够抓取敌人监视系统的“卡车”，

sentences.en: and basically put it into a dead zone.
sentences.zh: 并基本上将其置于死区。

sentences.en: Another thing that China did was in 2007, this is quite a while ago, they launched a missile up to about 530 miles, which is far into space,
sentences.zh: 中国做的另一件事是在 2007 年，那是很久以前的事了，他们发射了一枚导弹到约 530 英里高空，那已经深入太空，

sentences.en: and they destroyed another satellite that was in orbit, and it created an incredible cloud of space debris, the largest amount of space debris ever tracked.
sentences.zh: 摧毁了轨道上的另一颗卫星，制造了一团惊人的太空碎片云，这是有史以来追踪到的最大规模的太空碎片。

sentences.en: And it was quite a worrisome thing for the United States to see that
sentences.zh: 这对美国来说是一件非常令人担忧的事情，因为看到

sentences.en: China has the capacity to launch missiles from the ground that would destroy satellites and blow them up in low-Earth orbit.
sentences.zh: 中国有能力从地面发射导弹摧毁卫星，并在近地轨道上将其炸毁。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, both examples that you just described are much more targeted than what Russia is contemplating.
sentences.zh: 所以，你刚才描述的两个例子都比俄罗斯正在考虑的方案更具针对性。

sentences.en: You know, moving one satellite or using a missile to take one out, but the upshot is that China can disrupt our eyes and ears in space
sentences.zh: 你知道，移动一颗卫星或用导弹摧毁一颗，但结论是，中国可以干扰我们在太空中的眼睛和耳朵，

sentences.en: in a probably better, more efficient way than Russia.
sentences.zh: 其方式可能比俄罗斯更好、更有效。

sentences.en: And you're saying, given how much stuff they put up in space, they're more likely to already be able to do it than Russia, which is still trying to get to that point.
sentences.zh: 你是说，考虑到他们在太空中部署了这么多东西，他们比仍在努力达到这一点的俄罗斯更有可能已经具备了这种能力。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, the big difference between Russia and China right now as a space threat is that China is moving rapidly on both offensive and defensive systeMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，目前俄罗斯和中国作为太空威胁的最大区别在于，中国在进攻性和防御性系统上都在快速推进。

sentences.en: China is talking about building a state network of 13,000 satellites.
sentences.zh: 中国正在谈论建立一个由 13,000 颗卫星组成的国家网络。

sentences.en: That's, I mean, on a scale that's just completely outside of what Russia is attempting to do.
sentences.zh: 这……我的意思是，其规模完全超出了俄罗斯试图做的范围。

sentences.en: China is investing a lot more money, and it's moving much faster right now to put new systems in space.
sentences.zh: 中国投入了更多的资金，而且目前在太空中部署新系统的速度要快得多。

sentences.en: And those systems are both going to threaten United States satellites and also have a kind of a surveillance that would almost rival the United States.
sentences.zh: 这些系统既会威胁到美国的卫星，也具备一种几乎可以与美国相媲美的监视能力。

sentences.en: So I want to understand where the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以我想了解美国

sentences.en: sits in all of this, because when it comes to space, it feels like the thing that would make the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在这一切中处于什么位置，因为当谈到太空时，感觉会让美国

sentences.en: military so anxious about a rival's advancements in space is if we couldn't match them or we couldn't properly respond to them.
sentences.zh: 军方对竞争对手在太空中的进步感到焦虑的原因，是我们无法匹配他们，或者无法做出适当的回应。

sentences.en: So what is the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么美国

sentences.en: readiness right now to basically match or fight back against whatever Russia and China are doing in space?
sentences.zh: 目前是否有能力匹配或反击俄罗斯和中国在太空中的任何行动？

sentences.en: Everyone I talk to from the Pentagon and also former Pentagon officials all agree that the United States maintains clear dominance in space.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的每一位五角大楼人士以及前五角大楼官员都一致认为，美国在太空中保持着明显的统治地位。

sentences.en: It has more satellites for surveillance and missile targeting and missile defense than any other nation.
sentences.zh: 它拥有的用于监视、导弹瞄准和导弹防御的卫星数量超过了任何其他国家。

sentences.en: Both the United States and China have moved in a really rapid way into a new domain, and that is low Earth orbit.
sentences.zh: 美国和中国都以非常迅速的方式进入了一个新领域，那就是近地轨道。

sentences.en: That's about no greater than 1,200 miles off the surface of the Earth, and it's the area where SpaceX has put more than 5,000 satellites for its Starlink system.
sentences.zh: 那大约距离地球表面不超过1200英里，正是SpaceX为其“星链”系统部署了超过5000颗卫星的区域。

sentences.en: That's the focus right now is the flood-dead zone with lots of relatively cheap, quickly manufactured, easy-to-replace satellite systems,
sentences.zh: 目前的焦点就是这个低空死区，那里有大量相对廉价、快速制造、易于更换的卫星系统，

sentences.en: and the United States wants to put at least 1,000 satellites into low Earth orbit for its military purposes in the next several years.
sentences.zh: 而美国希望在未来几年内至少将1000颗卫星送入近地轨道，以实现其军事目的。

sentences.en: Among the many concerns that the American military has is that China is moving so rapidly right now to build out its own system
sentences.zh: 美国军方担忧的众多问题之一是，中国目前正如此迅速地建立自己的系统，

sentences.en: that unless the United States really accelerates what it's doing, that soon China could be close to matching what the U.S.
sentences.zh: 以至于除非美国真正加快行动步伐，否则中国很快就能接近追平美国

sentences.en: has in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空拥有的能力。

sentences.en: And that China now has enough surveillance capacity in space to target American military capacity in any type of a conflict.
sentences.zh: 而且中国现在在太空拥有足够的监视能力，可以在任何类型的冲突中瞄准美国的军事力量。

sentences.en: I mean, imagine, you know, the scenario where China decides to invade Taiwan and the United States decides that it's going to help defend Taiwan.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，试想一下，如果中国决定入侵台湾，而美国决定帮助保卫台湾，会发生什么？

sentences.en: If all of our military assets are immediately visible to China, they could be targeted even before they got to the Taiwan Straits.
sentences.zh: 如果我们所有的军事资产在第一时间就被中国尽收眼底，那么它们甚至在到达台湾海峡之前就可能成为目标。

sentences.en: Or even before they got within range to have a military engagement.
sentences.zh: 甚至在它们进入军事交战范围之前就可能被锁定。

sentences.en: And simultaneously, China's offensive space weapons were disabling American satellites so that the United States could no longer communicate.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，中国的进攻性太空武器可能会瘫痪美国的卫星，导致美国无法进行通信。

sentences.en: That's the fear that the military has right now is both of those things could suddenly happen if the United States is not building up its own space capacity
sentences.zh: 这就是军方目前的恐惧，即如果美国不加强自身的太空能力，这两件事可能会突然同时发生，

sentences.en: and its space weapons to disable Chinese satellites.
sentences.zh: 包括加强其瘫痪中国卫星的太空武器。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So the worry, and it's very specific, is that if China can achieve the same level of military prowess in space as the U.S., then the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个非常具体的担忧是，如果中国能在太空实现与美国同等水平的军事实力，那么美国

sentences.en: loses any power it has to deter China from doing something like invade Taiwan because we know, and they know that we know,
sentences.zh: 就失去了阻止中国采取类似入侵台湾行动的任何筹码，因为我们知道，而且他们也知道我们知道，

sentences.en: that they can basically shut down our systems before and during that invasion and make it impossible for us to stop them.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上可以在入侵前及入侵期间关闭我们的系统，使我们无法阻止他们。

sentences.en: It would severely degrade military capacity if they could wipe out a good share of our satellites.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能摧毁我们很大一部分卫星，那将严重削弱我们的军事能力。

sentences.en: And they're racing to try to avoid that.
sentences.zh: 而他们正在竞相避免这种情况发生。

sentences.en: So, Eric, what does it look like for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么，埃里克，美国为了避免中国达到美国目前的水平，

sentences.en: to race to avoid China meeting America's capabilities where they currently are?
sentences.zh: 会采取什么样的竞争姿态？

sentences.en: I mean, how does the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，美国

sentences.en: military do that?
sentences.zh: 军方是如何做到的？

sentences.en: Obviously, it would need to either slow China down or the U.S.
sentences.zh: 显然，它要么需要减缓中国的速度，要么美国

sentences.en: itself would need to speed up and race ahead of China.
sentences.zh: 自己需要加速并跑在中国前面。

sentences.en: There's two primary things that are happening right now.
sentences.zh: 目前主要有两件事正在发生。

sentences.en: One is to build out U.S.
sentences.zh: 一是建立美国的

sentences.en: offensive systems to disable Chinese or Russian satellites.
sentences.zh: 进攻性系统，以瘫痪中国或俄罗斯的卫星。

sentences.en: So that includes jamming systeMs.
sentences.zh: 这包括干扰系统。

sentences.en: They just signed a new contract to build new devices that could jam Chinese or Russian satellites and disrupt their signals.
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚签署了一份新合同，用于制造可以干扰中国或俄罗斯卫星并破坏其信号的新设备。

sentences.en: Laser systems that could destroy satellites from the ground or from space.
sentences.zh: 还有可以从地面或太空摧毁卫星的激光系统。

sentences.en: And also, other systems that did, just like the Chinese, that built a tug in space.
sentences.zh: 以及其他系统，就像中国人制造的太空拖船一样。

sentences.en: The United States potentially is going to build its own systems that could grab and disable other satellites in space.
sentences.zh: 美国可能也会制造自己的系统，能够在太空中捕获并瘫痪其他卫星。

sentences.en: The second piece of this plank is to build out a massive investment in space capacity by the United States
sentences.zh: 这一计划的第二部分是美国对太空能力进行大规模投资，

sentences.en: to build a whole new architecture in low Earth orbit with hundreds, if not more than a thousand satellites
sentences.zh: 在近地轨道构建一个全新的架构，部署数百甚至上千颗卫星，

sentences.en: that would be so many, so redundant, that you couldn't effectively disable the United States military capacity.
sentences.zh: 数量之多、冗余之高，以至于你无法有效地瘫痪美国的军事能力。

sentences.en: Because even if you were to shoot out a certain number of them, there would be yet more of them.
sentences.zh: 因为即使你击落了其中一部分，还会有更多的卫星补上来。

sentences.en: Sort of like Starlink right now, the SpaceX Starlink.
sentences.zh: 有点像现在的“星链”，SpaceX的“星链”。

sentences.en: If it loses a certain number of its 5,800 satellites, they just switch and they rebuild the network among the remaining satellites.
sentences.zh: 如果它损失了5800颗卫星中的一部分，它们只需切换并利用剩余的卫星重建网络即可。

sentences.en: Basically, everyone knows that the next time there's a major war with a major power, that there's going to be offensive activity in space.
sentences.zh: 基本上，大家都知道，下一次大国之间发生重大战争时，太空领域必然会出现进攻性活动。

sentences.en: And both sides are preparing for that.
sentences.zh: 双方都在为此做准备。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, what you're clearly describing is a new space race.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你所描述的显然是一场新的太空竞赛。

sentences.en: A space race that's about which of these three global superpowers can take out the other's satellites
sentences.zh: 这场太空竞赛关乎这三个全球超级大国中，谁能摧毁对方的卫星，

sentences.en: and use their satellites offensively and defensively to achieve military supremacy.
sentences.zh: 并利用自己的卫星进行进攻和防御，以实现军事霸权。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: I think that there's a new space race that's underway right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为一场新的太空竞赛正在进行中。

sentences.en: And it is more intense than at any time since really the 1960s when the United States and Russia were testing weapons in space for the first time.
sentences.zh: 而且它比20世纪60年代美国和俄罗斯首次在太空测试武器以来的任何时候都要激烈。

sentences.en: And it is very intense.
sentences.zh: 而且非常激烈。

sentences.en: And the increase in spending on space right now radically exceeds anything that the Navy or that, you know, the traditional Air Force or the Army is doing.
sentences.zh: 目前在太空上的支出增长幅度，远远超过了海军、传统空军或陆军的任何投入。

sentences.en: More dollars are pouring into space defense right now as a percentage increase.
sentences.zh: 目前投入太空防御的资金在百分比增长上非常惊人。

sentences.en: It's more than any other part of the military.
sentences.zh: 这比军方任何其他部门的投入都要多。

sentences.en: Eric, this makes me wonder how much the U.S.
sentences.zh: 埃里克，这让我不禁想问，美国

sentences.en: in its efforts to do those two things you just described out in space is ultimately reliant on contractors, the private sector, and in particular, Elon Musk, right?
sentences.zh: 在努力实现你刚才描述的那两项太空任务时，最终在多大程度上依赖于承包商、私营部门，特别是埃隆·马斯克？

sentences.en: This guy who has put so many satellites up in the sky, but who's mercurial and unique, to put it diplomatically.
sentences.zh: 这个把这么多卫星送上天，但用外交辞令来说，性格反复无常且独特的人。

sentences.en: So is the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么，美国

sentences.en: plan for staying ahead of both Russia and China to ultimately put more and more power in the hands of Elon Musk?
sentences.zh: 为了保持对俄罗斯和中国的领先地位，最终计划是把越来越多的权力交给埃隆·马斯克吗？

sentences.en: Right now, there's no question that SpaceX and Elon Musk plays an extraordinarily dominant role in the ability to launch to orbit.
sentences.zh: 目前毫无疑问，SpaceX和埃隆·马斯克在进入轨道的能力方面发挥着极其主导的作用。

sentences.en: And the military is excessively reliant on SpaceX.
sentences.zh: 军方对SpaceX的依赖程度过高了。

sentences.en: So at this moment, it's an uncomfortable sort of domination by SpaceX.
sentences.zh: 所以目前，这是一种令人不安的SpaceX式统治。

sentences.en: Of the 9,400 objects in orbit right now, 5,235 of them are SpaceX Starlink satellites.
sentences.zh: 在目前轨道上的9400个物体中，有5235个是SpaceX的“星链”卫星。

sentences.en: So almost all of the satellites in orbit that from any nation in the world are Elon Musk.
sentences.zh: 所以世界上任何国家在轨道上的卫星几乎都是埃隆·马斯克的。

sentences.en: But the Department of Defense realizes that it can't be so reliant upon one company for launch.
sentences.zh: 但国防部意识到，它不能在发射方面如此依赖一家公司。

sentences.en: And so the Pentagon is also signing contracts with small launch companies to quickly be able to put military satellites into space with just a few days notice.
sentences.zh: 因此，五角大楼也正在与小型发射公司签署合同，以便在接到通知后的几天内就能迅速将军事卫星送入太空。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And so there's a lot of money that's being spent to build out this capacity.
sentences.zh: 所以为了建立这种能力，投入了大量的资金。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So what you're really saying is that this new space race is going to come with and foster a new space military industrial complex that's going to be the recipient of many billions,
sentences.zh: 所以你真正想说的是，这场新的太空竞赛将会伴随并催生一个新的太空军工复合体，它将获得数百亿，

sentences.en: maybe trillions of dollars in taxpayer money.
sentences.zh: 甚至数万亿纳税人的钱。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, the United States is already in the middle of an incredible explosion in the commercial
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，美国已经处于商业

sentences.en: space industry because the number of commercial launches is growing at a really crazy rate.
sentences.zh: 航天工业的惊人爆发之中，因为商业发射的数量正在以非常疯狂的速度增长。

sentences.en: And in the entire world right now, there are approximately 10,000 objects in orbit.
sentences.zh: 目前全世界大约有10000个物体在轨道上。

sentences.en: And within the next 10 years, the expectation is going to be something like 25,000 satellites in orbit.
sentences.zh: 预计在未来10年内，轨道上的卫星数量将达到25000颗左右。

sentences.en: So there's a huge boom right now in the space industry globally.
sentences.zh: 所以全球航天工业目前正处于巨大的繁荣期。

sentences.en: So, Eric, when I step back, it feels like the inevitable outcome of this new space race,
sentences.zh: 那么，埃里克，当我退一步看时，感觉这场新太空竞赛的必然结果，

sentences.en: this weapons space race is a very potentially expensive version of what we already have, which is that famous concept of mutually assured destruction, right?
sentences.zh: 这场武器太空竞赛，很可能是一个非常昂贵版本的我们已经拥有的东西，即那个著名的“相互保证毁灭”的概念，对吧？

sentences.en: It's this idea that all three of these countries have nuclear weapons, and it keeps us all in check, Russia, China, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这就是说，这三个国家都拥有核武器，这让我们所有人——俄罗斯、中国、美国——都受到制约。

sentences.en: We don't attack each other directly because we all fear that the other country attacked would fire back in obliterating ways that would never make it worth it.
sentences.zh: 我们不会直接攻击对方，因为我们都担心被攻击的国家会以毁灭性的方式反击，这让攻击变得得不偿失。

sentences.en: And so, isn't that kind of where we're headed with this battle over space?
sentences.zh: 那么，这场太空之战不正是朝着这个方向发展吗？

sentences.en: All three countries are going to be spending a tremendous amount of money eventually to reach
sentences.zh: 这三个国家最终都会投入巨额资金来达到

sentences.en: some kind of loose parity that prevents us all from doing something really horrible to the other country.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上的松散平衡，从而防止我们所有人对另一个国家做出真正可怕的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, I sort of reject your premise.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我有点反对你的前提。

sentences.en: And I think that, in fact, the thing that the United States is concerned about is it has had such a massive advantage in space for so long, and it's been so central to our global
sentences.zh: 我认为，事实上，美国所担心的是，它在太空领域长期拥有巨大的优势，而这对于我们的全球

sentences.en: military supremacy.
sentences.zh: 军事霸权至关重要。

sentences.en: And suddenly, if you have another nation that's kind of walking in and becoming your rival in that environment, I mean, that's really worrisome to the American military.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，如果有另一个国家介入并成为你在该环境中的竞争对手，我的意思是，这对美国军方来说是非常令人担忧的。

sentences.en: And they're determined to prevent China from matching the United States military capacity in space.
sentences.zh: 他们决心阻止中国在太空领域追平美国的军事能力。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: You're saying this is not about the three countries ever achieving parity.
sentences.zh: 你是说这根本不是关于这三个国家实现平衡的问题。

sentences.en: It's about the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而是关于美国

sentences.en: ensuring that parity is never achieved.
sentences.zh: 确保这种平衡永远不会实现。

sentences.en: Because if it's achieved, then everything changes.
sentences.zh: 因为一旦实现，一切都会改变。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think that basically the Pentagon wants to ensure that it can maintain dominance in space and not
sentences.zh: 我认为五角大楼基本上是想确保它能保持在太空的统治地位，而不仅仅是

sentences.en: just parity, because space-based dominance is so vital to the way that the United States military has operated for years now.
sentences.zh: 平衡，因为基于太空的统治地位对于美国军方多年来的运作方式至关重要。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 即使在黑胶唱片时代的夜店里做DJ时，你每晚也要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个活生生的、充满50年历史精美文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times Games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《连接》游戏。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天负责创作《拼字蜜蜂》和《字母盒》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人那样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏吧。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, President Biden summoned House and Senate leaders to the White House in an attempt to avoid the latest potential government shutdown.
sentences.zh: 周二，拜登总统召集参众两院领导人前往白宫，试图避免政府再次面临停摆。

sentences.en: That shutdown, which could begin at midnight on Saturday, would be the result of strident
sentences.zh: 这次停摆可能在周六午夜开始，其起因是众议院共和党人

sentences.en: demands from House Republicans who have attached right-wing policies to basic spending bills that have made them impossible to pass in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 提出的强硬要求，他们将右翼政策附加到基本支出法案上，导致这些法案在参议院根本无法通过。

sentences.en: We believe that we can get to agreement on these issues and prevent a government shutdown, and that's our first responsibility.
sentences.zh: 我们相信我们可以在这些问题上达成一致并防止政府停摆，这是我们的首要责任。

sentences.en: As he left the White House, Republican House Speaker Mike Johnson expressed optimism that a shutdown would be averted.
sentences.zh: 离开白宫时，众议院共和党议长迈克·约翰逊表示，乐观地认为停摆可以避免。

sentences.en: And we have been working in good faith around the clock every single day for months and weeks
sentences.zh: 我们几个月来、几周来，每天都在真诚地全天候工作，

sentences.en: and over the last several days, quite literally around the clock, to get that job done.
sentences.zh: 在过去几天里，确实是全天候工作，以完成这项任务。

sentences.en: And in a rebuke to President Biden, more than 100,000 Democratic voters in Michigan cast protest
sentences.zh: 作为对拜登总统的抗议，密歇根州超过10万名民主党选民投下了

sentences.en: ballots that declared themselves uncommitted to express disapproval of the president's handling of the war in Gaza.
sentences.zh: “不表态”选票，以表达对总统处理加沙战争方式的不满。

sentences.en: That number far exceeded the goal of 10,000 uncommitted ballots that activists had set for themselves and could spell trouble for Biden in the general election.
sentences.zh: 这一数字远远超过了活动人士设定的1万张“不表态”选票的目标，可能会给拜登在大选中带来麻烦。

sentences.en: Michigan is a key swing state where Biden defeated Donald Trump in 2020.
sentences.zh: 密歇根州是拜登在2020年击败唐纳德·特朗普的关键摇摆州。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Michael Simon Johnson and Carlos Prieto, with help from Will
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由迈克尔·西蒙·约翰逊和卡洛斯·普列托制作，威尔·里德和穆吉·扎迪德提供协助。

sentences.en: Reid and Muj Zadid.
sentences.zh: 由莱克西·迪奥编辑，包含玛丽安·洛萨诺、丹·鲍威尔和帕特·麦卡斯克创作的原创音乐，并由艾丽莎·莫克斯利进行工程制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lexi Diao, contains original music by Marian Lozano, Dan Powell and Pat McCusker, and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯费克创作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansferk of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的内容。
